input.note:
**Root Cause: Bad pricing rule "BF-2026-STACKED" introduced in rules-admin revision 8841**

This is *not* a Kubernetes issue. Kubernetes is behaving correctly — it is restarting the containers because the application is crashing at startup, which triggers `CrashLoopBackOff` with exponential backoff [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-0].

---

**Evidence:**

Both pods (`pricing-engine-74d9c6b8f-5tnwh` and `pricing-engine-74d9c6b8f-jq7lc`) show:
- Status: `CrashLoopBackOff`, 12 restarts each, last terminated with **exit code 2**
- Identical panic in the logs on every startup:

```
2026-05-22T14:07:31Z INFO fetched 1,204 active rules from rules-admin (revision 8841)
2026-05-22T14:07:31Z INFO compiling rule BF-2026-STACKED (tiers=3, stacking=true)
panic: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3

goroutine 1 [running]:
github.com/acme/pricing/internal/rules.(*TierTable).Lookup(...)
    /src/internal/rules/tiers.go:88
github.com/acme/pricing/internal/rules.(*Compiler).compileStacked(...)
    /src/internal/rules/compile.go:214
```

The engine starts, fetches rules from `rules-admin` at **revision 8841**, then immediately panics trying to compile rule **BF-2026-STACKED** due to an off-by-one index error (accessing index 3 in a 3-element array). The image (`4.11.3`, deployed 2026-04-27) has not changed; the new bad rule in rules-admin is what changed today. The `CrashLoopBackOff` state is a direct result of an application error causing the container to exit [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-1].

---

**Fix (no Kubernetes changes needed):**

1. **In `rules-admin`**, find and fix or delete the rule **BF-2026-STACKED**. The rule appears to declare `tiers=3` but the tier data only has 3 entries (indices 0–2), and the compiler is trying to look up index 3. Either:
   - Reduce the tier count to match the actual data, **or**
   - Add the missing 4th tier entry, **or**
   - Delete the rule entirely to unblock the service immediately.
2. Once the rule is corrected in rules-admin, the pricing-engine pods will fetch the updated rules on the next restart and start successfully — no pod/deployment changes are required.
3. To speed up recovery after the fix, you can manually delete the two crashing pods (`kubectl delete pod pricing-engine-74d9c6b8f-5tnwh pricing-engine-74d9c6b8f-jq7lc -n pricing`) so they restart immediately rather than waiting for the backoff timer [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-2].
